After two months of tough engineering and testing, including some mosquito bites, native Tesla phone key support is now working on our iOS app. 🎉

To celebrate, please enjoy this very candid video of the first successful test, captured tonight by our house security cameras. 🤣

Video

Walk Away Automatic Lock was also tested and successfully completed for the first time. 🚗🔒

Phone Key has been the #1 requested feature of all Tesla third-party apps and was the missing puzzle piece for releasing our Apple Watch companion app with full Phone Key support. ⌚

Video

Whether 1AM or 1PM, I’ve been working dilligently to get this app officially released on the App Store and off of TestFlight.

A trove of new features, including Phone Key, will be released to testers this weekend and I’m excited for this to be in everyone’s hands very soon. 🫡

Some thoughts from our founder.


Tyler Corsair (@tylercorsair)

With Vehiclescope (@teslascope / @vehiclescope), I've always striven to ensure that each and every customer service request is read and responded to by me.

Being involved with every aspect of the product, from customer service, development, infrastructure, marketing, social media, and legal, keeps me connected with the community and customers that my products couldn't exist without.

At scale and with larger products, I know that this isn't feasible and that dedicated customer support teams are necessary. With another company I am launching this year, this will very much be unavoidable at some point.

But it will always be paramount to me that feedback is condensed, organized, and that it makes its way to my inbox. If my communities and customers no longer feel heard, I consider that a failure as an executive.

Hold me to that.



— https://nitter.net/tylercorsair/status/2089501530428961115#m
